iteration_history.candidate: The system shall prevent code injection attacks through the evaluation of externally-supplied input in the shell component.

issues: The evidence describes a code pattern that was detected and remediated, but does not state what behaviour changed for an observer or what the system now guarantees.

The requirement prescribes a defence mechanism—'prevent code injection'—rather than stating an observable behaviour. The evidence says only that eval() was present and has been addressed; it does not describe what callers of the shell component can now do or rely on.

The evidence does not establish whether the remediation eliminates the vulnerability entirely, mitigates it partially, or changes the attack surface. Without knowing what the fix was, the requirement cannot be grounded: it asserts a conclusion rather than a fact about the system.
revision_instructions: The evidence names only a problem—the presence of eval()—and says it was remediated, but does not state what the applied remedy was or what the system now does differently. A requirement grounded in this evidence cannot assert what vulnerability is prevented; it can only state facts about what changed that an observer could verify. Without access to the remediation itself, no requirement can be written that goes beyond restating the detection rule.
